**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** In today's society people think it is more important to do the sciences as there are ready jobs in the industries. Write a letter to a friend stating the importance of the Arts subjects (which is the series you opted for). You may want to describe a society that is made only of scientists and the disadvantages of life in a purely scientific society. Describe five advantages why literature, history, arts and languages are important to our society. Your name is Ayukeng, you are from GHS Ekpoh in the West Region; your post office box number is 777.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC série A évalue à la fois le respect du format imposé (lettre personnelle, composition narrative/argumentative, discours) et la qualité du contenu. Le sujet proposant un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun des trois sujets proposés.

## Topic 1 - Personal letter (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Ayukeng
GHS Ekpoh
West Region
P.O. Box 777

Dear friend,

I hope this letter finds you well. I wanted to share some thoughts with you about a debate that has been on my mind lately: the growing belief that only the sciences matter, while subjects like literature, history, arts and languages are treated as secondary.

Imagine, for a moment, a society made up only of scientists and engineers. Such a society could certainly build impressive machines and cure diseases, but it would struggle to answer far more human questions: how should we live together, what do we owe one another, how do we make sense of our past and imagine our future? Without historians, we would forget the lessons of our own mistakes. Without writers and artists, we would lose the stories and images that help us understand emotions science cannot measure. Without linguists, communication across cultures would suffer, and much of our shared humanity would remain unspoken.

This is precisely why I chose the Arts series, and why I believe it deserves far more respect than it currently receives. First, literature develops empathy, teaching us to see the world through other people's eyes. Second, history equips us to understand the present by studying the causes and consequences of past events. Third, languages open doors to other cultures and to international opportunities that many scientific careers alone cannot offer. Fourth, the arts nurture creativity, a skill increasingly valued even within technical and scientific fields. Fifth, philosophy and related humanities subjects train us to reason critically about ethics and values, questions no laboratory experiment can settle alone.

A balanced society needs both scientists and humanists working side by side. I hope this helps you see why I am proud of the path I have chosen.

Your friend,
Ayukeng

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** It is Christmas. Your uncle just arrived from America and distributed smart android mobile phones to everyone in the house as compensation for good performances at school. Your younger brother who is only 14 also had a phone. Write a composition indicating how the phone can be disadvantageous for this young man who is in a *Troisieme* class in college.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Composition (modèle, environ 260 mots)

This Christmas, my uncle arrived from America with a suitcase full of smart android phones, one for every member of the family, including my younger brother, who is only fourteen and still in Troisieme. At first, everyone was thrilled, but looking more closely at my brother's situation, I began to see real reasons for concern.

At fourteen, a smartphone can easily become more of a distraction than a tool. My brother now spends hours scrolling through social media and watching videos late into the night, time that used to go into his homework and revision. His sleep has suffered, and so, unsurprisingly, has his concentration in class.

A smartphone at that age also exposes him to content he is not yet mature enough to process critically: violent videos, inappropriate images, and strangers online who may not have his best interests at heart. Without proper parental controls or guidance, a young teenager can easily wander into corners of the internet meant for adults.

There is also a social cost. Constant phone use can replace real face-to-face interaction with family and friends, weakening the very relationships a young person needs most during adolescence. Finally, an expensive phone can make a young student a target, whether for theft or for the pressure to constantly compare himself to others online.

None of this means my brother should never have a phone. It simply means that, at fourteen, he needs clear limits, supervision, and guidance on how to use such a powerful tool responsibly, rather than being handed unrestricted access all at once.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** You live in a part of town where garbage is quite abundant. Plastics and other used items have blocked the drainage system. You are the president of the youth association in that neighbourhood and you think something should be done to improve the image of that neighbourhood. Write a speech addressing the problem and describing five things the youth or the community can do to help improve the situation.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Speech (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Ladies and gentlemen, fellow youths,

As president of our neighbourhood's youth association, I stand before you today because our environment is sending us a clear warning: garbage, especially plastic, has blocked our drainage system, and if we do nothing, the consequences for our community will only get worse.

Every rainy season, water that should flow freely through our drains instead backs up, flooding streets and compounds, because plastic bottles, bags and other waste have clogged the very channels meant to carry it away. This is not simply an eyesore; it is a threat to our health and our safety.

I therefore propose five concrete actions we, as youths, can take. First, let us organise a monthly community clean-up day, focused specifically on clearing drains of plastic and debris. Second, let us set up clearly marked collection points where households can dispose of plastic waste properly, rather than in gutters or empty plots. Third, let us go from house to house to raise awareness about the dangers of blocked drainage, especially during flooding season. Fourth, let us partner with local shops to reduce the use of single-use plastic bags in our neighbourhood. Fifth, let us work with local authorities to ensure that collected waste is actually transported to proper disposal sites, rather than simply moved from one corner of the neighbourhood to another.

None of these steps require significant funding, only our collective will and consistent effort. Let us restore the image of our neighbourhood, one clean drain at a time.

Thank you.

### Piège à éviter
Dans un discours (Topic 3), l'erreur fréquente est de lister les actions proposées sans les numéroter ni les structurer clairement ("First", "Second"...) : un discours efficace organise toujours ses propositions de façon visible pour l'auditoire.

### Conseil
Pour un sujet demandant un nombre précis d'éléments (ici cinq avantages ou cinq actions), compte-les explicitement au brouillon avant de rédiger : cela évite d'en oublier un ou d'en proposer un de trop, ce qui peut coûter des points si le barème exige un nombre exact.
